papers.title: Multi-label Learning for Predicting the Activities of Antimicrobial Peptides
Classifier-driven generative adversarial networks for enhanced antimicrobial peptide design

aliases: Multi-label learning model for AMP activity prediction
models.architecture_or_algorithm: Weighted K-nearest neighbor (WKnn) for label score computation, followed by multiple linear regression (MLR) to incorporate label correlations and predict final label set.
models.input_features: Amino acid composition (AAC, 20-dim) + dipeptide composition (DC, 400-dim) = 420-dimensional feature vector
models.dataset_source_or_link: APD database (May 2016) filtered to 2222 AMPs with 5 activities; APD3 available at https://aps.unmc.edu/AP/
models.candidate_reason: Novel multi-label method for AMP activity prediction with clear methodology and publicly available dataset (APD), suitable for inclusion in benchmark comparison.
blocking_issues: No code or web server available
models.representative_reason: A multi-label method for AMP activity prediction using amino acid composition; suitable as a baseline for multi-label classification.

models.task_type: antimicrobial peptide design (generative model with classifier)
models.architecture_or_algorithm: Classifier-driven GAN with ESM2-based classifier integrated into loss function; generator produces peptide sequences, classifier evaluates antimicrobial probability.
models.input_features: peptide sequences (10-50 residues), structural annotations from Porter 5
models.candidate_reason: Primarily a generative model; classifier may be reused for prediction but not directly benchmarked as a standalone AMP predictor.
blocking_issues: Generative model, not a direct AMP predictor
Classifier weights not explicitly provided as standalone predictor
models.representative_reason: cdGAN represents a classifier-driven generative approach for AMP design; could serve as a representative for generative models in design tasks.

repositories.name: amp_de_novo_design_cdGAN
repositories.evidence: GitHub repository linked in the paper: https://github.com/aretiz/amp_de_novo_design_cdGAN.

datasets.dataset_source: APD database (https://aps.unmc.edu/AP/), filtered to 2222 AMPs with 5 activities
datasets.negative_samples: none (multi-label dataset, no explicit negative class)

datasets.dataset_source: APD3 for AMPs, reviewed UniProt for non-AMPs, clustered with MMseqs2 at 50% identity
datasets.deduplication_method: MMseqs2 clustering at 50% sequence identity for non-AMPs; average pairwise similarity 0.2
datasets.split_method: not explicitly described (likely used for GAN training)

model_dataset_links.evidence: Dataset used for leave-one-out cross-validation of multi-label activity prediction.
Dataset used to train the classifier-driven GAN for AMP design.

metrics.usage: Multi-label evaluation of AMP activity prediction
metrics.evidence: Paper reports Hamming loss, one-error, coverage, ranking loss, average precision.

important_evidence: Multi-label WKnn-MLR proposes a novel method for predicting five AMP activities simultaneously, using AAC and dipeptide composition features.
cdGAN introduces a classifier-driven GAN framework that integrates ESM2-based classifier into the loss function for AMP design; code and dataset are available on GitHub.
Both papers rely on APD-derived datasets; the first uses a filtered multi-label set (2222 AMPs), the second uses a balanced APD3+UniProt set (5200 sequences).
uncertainties: Is the multi-label WKnn-MLR model available as a web server or code?
Does the cdGAN classifier (ESM2-based) function as a standalone AMP prediction model worthy of separate benchmarking?
Are the filtered datasets from both papers directly downloadable from the APD version used or from the GitHub repository?
